messages:
inc-bot: INCIDENT OPENED (Sev 2) — elevated 5xx rate detected on canary routing endpoint 'router-v3-experiment'. Auto-created thread.

maria: heads up — canary is showing consistent 502s for prompt routing requests after 10:12 UTC. spike on the new endpoint only (not stable-router).

alex: getting paged, linking perf dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/routing?from=now-15m to=now

sam: I’m taking this. oncall here — investigating logs and traces now. can anyone confirm which release pushed the experiment?

maria: deploy tag is deploy-2026-03-15-routerv3-canary, rolled out ~09:58 UTC to 10% canary. change was 'support multi-turn function_call routing' plus new inference endpoint path /v2/prompt-route-experiment.

luis: looking at the canary pods — they return 502 when payload contains a 'function_call' field. stack: router service -> router-v3 -> routing-layer -> model-gateway. error shows: "UpstreamError: model-gateway returned 502: invalid_request" repeated.

sam: paste of recent log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T10:11:23Z ERROR router-v3 request_id=abc123 UpstreamError: model-gateway returned 502 - invalid route for payload with function_call
2026-03-15T10:11:23Z DEBUG router-v3 payload={"prompt":"...","function_call":{"name":"search","args":{}}}
```

jenny: product question — are customers impacted or just internal canaries? any enterprise clients routing to experiment?

maria: we have a small percentage of traffic from a couple of customers who opted into the experiment in prod (opt-in flag). early signal shows 14 requests failed across 2 enterprise tenants (they're on dedicated capacity but routing policy opted experiment).

sam: marking customer impact: yes, low-volume but includes paying tenants. creating incident impact note. paging SRE lead.

luis: probable cause hypothesis: new endpoint expects a rewritten function_call schema and returns 502 when unrecognized. fallback logic didn't trigger for canary, so requests aren't redirected to stable-router.

alex: past incidents runbook for routing failures suggests either rollback the canary or flip the feature flag kill-switch that gates routing to the experiment. since this is a cross-tenant opt-in experiment we should toggle the FF first (less blast radius).

sam: agreed. can someone with FF perms toggle 'exp_router_v3' -> false? we have a LaunchDarkly integration but internal fast-path is ff-service. commands below (use ops creds):
```bash
# toggle via ff-service (internal)
curl -X POST https://ff-api.internal/flags/exp_router_v3/toggle -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' -d '{\"enabled\":false}'
# or via KD (LaunchDarkly): ldctl set exp_router_v3 false --env=prod
```

luis: I can flip it, executing now.

launchdarkly-bot: Received request to change flag 'exp_router_v3' by luis. Initiating toggle.

luis: done — I toggled 'exp_router_v3' -> false from ff-service UI at 10:20:13 UTC.

launchdarkly-bot: Flag 'exp_router_v3' set to false (actor: luis). All edge nodes should receive update within ~30s.

ops-bot: Observability note: config propagation started.

sam: running quick validation checks against canary traffic and replaying the failing payloads. initial checks show 502s dropping immediately. running a small synthetic test — sending payload with function_call to stable-router endpoint.

sam: synthetic result: stable-router returns 200 and completes call. canary still returns occasional 502 but decreasing (propagation lag).

maria: traffic back to baseline for error rate on routing: error-rate 0.3% (was 6.7% at peak). linking updated graph: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/routing?from=now-30m to=now

jenny: good. product will notify affected customers with note: we experienced transient failed requests for experimental routing; we've disabled the experiment and are monitoring. drafting email now.

sam: decision: do NOT roll back cluster yet — kill-switch toggle fixed the immediate customer impact and we need time for a full root-cause. setting incident status: mitigated, monitoring.

maria: creating a follow-up task for eng-runtime to reproduce schema mismatch and add a defensive fallback to route to stable-router when model-gateway returns 502 for function_call payloads.

alex: prepping postmortem and flagging infra for deeper deploy-test coverage on new endpoint route tests.

tao: I'll take overnight watch for two hours then hand off to next oncall at 18:00 UTC. tagging monitoring alert to ensure no re-enable activity.

sam: handing off to tao — all action items and commands in this thread. please escalate if error-rate >1% for 15m.

tao: ack. I have read-only access to ff-service and will confirm flag remains off.

maria: next steps: 1) eng-runtime recreate locally + unit test for function_call schema 2) platform to add canary-level fallback 3) postmortem with timeline + customer impact + remediation.

jenny: assigning comms: I'll send the customer note and schedule a join request for any affected customers who want a post-incident call. :mailbox_with_mail:

inc-bot: INCIDENT STATUS UPDATED — mitigated. Severity downgraded to Sev 3 while monitoring for 2 hours.

sam: closing pager for immediate action. leaving thread open for postmortem activities. :white_check_mark:

tao: monitoring logs for 30m. no further spikes observed at 10:48 UTC. will update if anything changes.

maria: thanks everyone — great quick coordination. I'll file the postmortem draft in docs/incidents/postmortems/ after initial RCA.
